title: FREE Beta Access to AI Trading App. I built a desktop/mobile trading app supporting Robinhood and Public currently, and I’m looking for testers
author: BFitch85
selftext:
Hey everyone, I’m the developer of **trelic**, a Windows trading app that currently connects Claude with your Robinhood or Public account.

You can describe trading strategies in plain English, have the app analyze market data and propose trades, and review orders before submitting them. It also includes paper trading, configurable trade limits, position tracking, and optional automation.

The app is **free during beta testing**, and I’m looking for feedback on setup, usability, bugs, and features you would actually use.

Here’s how access works:

* Create an account and complete a $0 Stripe checkout.
* No credit card is required.
* Your activation key arrives by email.
* There is no automatic conversion to a paid subscription.

The trelic software license is free during beta. You provide your own Anthropic API key and pay any API usage and applicable brokerage charges separately.

There is no beta end date yet. I’ll announce changes before free access ends. If paid plans launch, you would need to explicitly choose a plan and enter payment details.

This is beta software that can place real trades when live trading is enabled. Start with paper trading while you get familiar with it. There are no promises of profitable results.

If you try it, I’d especially appreciate hearing where setup gets confusing, what breaks, and what would make the app more useful to you.

[Get free beta access](https://trelictech.com/pricing.html) (if you don't want to click links, go to trelictech . com and navigate to trading app > pricing)

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: For trelic's optional automation, a useful paper-trading test would be a Robinhood or Public order that gets accepted but whose acknowledgement never reaches the app. If Claude retries, can the app reconcile the original order before submitting another? I'd also want configurable trade limits to count pending orders, so two submissions can't each pass against the same remaining allowance. A visible order-status log would make that failure case much easier for beta testers to report.

replies.author: BFitch85
replies.body:
Submission attempts count toward the daily limit, and confirmations run one at a time so they can’t use the same remaining allowance.

I ended up double checking the successful order not reaching the app. Had to edit Robinhood side, the next build adds automatic recovery for both brokers. Public checks the original order ID first. Robinhood retries the unchanged request with the same saved reference, using its documented duplicate protection. Retries are limited and recheck current risk limits.

I like the order-status timeline idea, it already had a "Pending Orders" section on home screen and "Orders" section in Analytics tab (now where the order timeline lives), so I integrated this into the newest update.   
  
So far the simulated failure tests are passing, but I haven’t tested the lost-response case yet with a real order.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the review-before-submit step is what I'd fight hardest to keep, even for the testers who ask you to remove it. the moment optional automation can skip the review screen, your first bug report will be a real fill somebody didn't want. also worth saying plainly which mode you're in, paper or live, on every screen. people forget. which broker gave you more trouble on the paper side, robinhood or public?

replies.author: BFitch85
replies.body:
The fully autonomous mode is an opt-in toggle in settings that also has a confirmation pop-up after toggle. Same with switching from paper mode to live trading. I can’t attach an image here, but there’s a red “AUTO MODE” indicator when automation is enabled and a yellow “PAPER MODE” indicator when paper trading is enabled. Both stay visible on every tab.

My paper-mode testing has been with Robinhood so far, so I can’t really compare the two there. Robinhood has been a better fit for the market data I need. It also needed more work on the lost-response recovery.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the double confirm on paper to live is the right amount of friction. the red AUTO MODE badge is good, I'd just make sure it survives on the mobile layout too, that's where people fat-finger toggles.

replies.author: BFitch85
replies.body:
I agree with that. On mobile it's just in a bubble at the top of the app. I can look into making it more noticeable. 

Currently it's written so the app can't toggle autonomous or paper-mode. It can review every trade (like if you're on the go, you can allow mobile notifications in app and get a push notification to review a new order), and you can create new tasks and start/stop them. 

Desktop and mobile both have a "kill switch" too if everything is going bad, you click it and it will stop all tasks, pause recovery attempts, exit automation mode, and disconnect from the brokerage.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: push to review, toggles desktop only, is the right split. the phone gets the actions you can undo and the desktop gets the ones you can't.

replies.author: BFitch85
replies.body:
Thanks! 

Would be open to any more suggestions or criticisms if you check it out!

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body:
The 'review before submitting' step is the right default for a beta, especially with live trading enabled from day one, since even a well-tuned prompt can misread ambiguous market data and propose something you didn't actually mean. Curious how you're handling rate limiting and cost control though, since 'describe strategy in plain English, app analyzes and proposes trades' sounds like it could burn through API calls fast if someone's running it continuously rather than on-demand, especially with users providing their own Anthropic key. Also worth being explicit in the app somewhere about what happens if Claude's response is ambiguous or contradicts itself between two calls, does it default to no action, or surface the disagreement to the user before they approve anything? That failure mode matters more than the happy path for something that can place real trades.

Building something adjacent in this space myself, EventTrader, focused more on event-driven signals and agent hookups than direct brokerage execution, but always interested to compare notes with people building in the same lane [https://claude.ai/artifact/VuwYE2KYrtzMdwyEpvA9wH](https://claude.ai/artifact/VuwYE2KYrtzMdwyEpvA9wH)
